mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1600 units signals increased consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence indices
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1600, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1.5% eases monetary conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of other market conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment (UNRATE) falls below 3.2% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in a month, the combined labor market strength predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and SPX correlation
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both labor market conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 2% YoY signals increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 45% of instances when INDPRO YoY growth > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real disposable personal income (RSAFS) growth below -2% YoY indicates decreased consumer spending power, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical RSAFS and consumer spending correlation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 55% of instances when RSAFS YoY growth < -2%, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) growth rate exceeds 3% YoY, the combined inflationary pressure predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to potential monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth, regardless of other conditions, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to its persistent correlation with economic activity.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or PAYEMS growth does not significantly correlate with SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: GDP (GDPC1) growth above 3% YoY, combined with housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 units, signals robust economic activity, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 3-year rolling window.
